clue.text: Times going after Foreign Office and Chancellor – they're out for blood?

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the Foreign Office
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'
Jeremy Hunt, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Newspaper commentators going after the Foreign Office and the Chancellor, hungry for a political kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper chasing a story, but it is the multiplication sign; Hunt was Chancellor of the Exchequer in 2023.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting party with hounds chasing a fox is a group seeking blood; the question mark flags the loose, playful description.

clue.text: Adjusting one leg a bit on the table

indicators.note: adjusting something rearranges it, so the following words are reordered

blocks.note: the ten letters of these four words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone levelling a wobbly table by tweaking one of its legs slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal that is on the table is open for discussion, so its terms can still be negotiated.

clue.text: Fed sons stew

blocks.note: Fed is this puzzle's setter, so the setter's name stands for 'me'
s is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Fed feeds the boys a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym; here Fed, this puzzle's setter, means ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew and a mess are both a confused, muddled state, and a mess is also an old word for a dish of food.

clue.text: Scientist's flight-component placed on two birds with clipped wings

indicators.note: clipping trims the edges, so the word after it loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: a flight of stairs is made up of steps
two birds: a hen and a hawk
wings with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A component of a flight, as in an aircraft, fitted to two birds whose wings have been clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests birds or aircraft, but here it is a flight of stairs; 'with' just joins the clipped wings on after the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Hawking was the British theoretical physicist known for his work on black holes.

clue.text: Made during a concert with, say, Robin Williams essentially entering profession

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept
entering means going inside, so these letters sit within the other pieces

blocks.note: a live recording is one made during a concert
the two middle letters of the eight-letter name
Robin Hood is an example of a Robin

explanation.surface: Robin Williams performing at a live gig as his main line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robin Williams' reads as the actor, but the two names do separate jobs: one is an example of a famous outlaw's first name, the other gives up its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A livelihood is the means by which a person earns a living, which is what a profession provides.

clue.text: Boots, maybe Hush Puppies' first with zip set in

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word before it is used
set in means placed inside the surrounding letters

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
zip means nothing, nought, the letter O
opening letter of Puppies

explanation.surface: Footwear talk: boots, perhaps Hush Puppies, with a zip fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Hush Puppies are a shoe brand, so 'Boots' looks like footwear, but Boots is the British chain of chemists and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots is a well-known British high-street pharmacy chain, an example of a retail outlet; 'maybe' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Husband joining a navy ship under European control

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the ship below European, so that piece comes second

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for husband
taken as written
the Royal Navy
standard abbreviation for European
steamship, the standard ship prefix

explanation.surface: A husband signs up to serve on a naval vessel commanded by a European power.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places the ship below European, so E comes before SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To harness something is to bring it under control and put it to use, as with a river's power.

clue.text: Spooner's only visitor died

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so two words here trade their starts

blocks.note: only visitor is one guest; swapping the w and g sounds gives the phrase

explanation.surface: Spooner's lone visitor has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone west is an old idiom for having died, from the setting sun.

clue.text: Where copper needs to go to get old-school jazz fan up for relations?

blocks.clueFragment: Where copper needs to go to get old-school jazz fan
blocks.note: surface reading: a puzzle about where a police officer must be sent
setter's reading: copper is PC, and placing PC inside the slang word for police spells HEPCAT, a dated term for a jazz fan

explanation.surface: A riddle about where to send a policeman to find a retro jazz lover who is keen for a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: HEAT is slang for the police, and PC put in HEAT gives HEPCAT. So where copper must go is IN HEAT, which also means ready to mate.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal in heat is in its fertile period and receptive to mating, hence up for sexual relations.

clue.text: Takes horse say, and climbs rapidly

blocks.note: first meaning: injects a drug such as heroin, which is slang 'horse'
second meaning: rises fast, as prices or a plant do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes horse' sounds like riding, but horse is slang for heroin, and to take it by needle is to shoot up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both injecting a drug intravenously and rising sharply, as a growing teenager does.

clue.text: Develop play oddly following cross into goal

indicators.note: oddly means taking only the letters in odd positions of the word before
into means the preceding letters are placed inside the next word

blocks.note: a cross is the shape X
first and third letters of play
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football team building play erratically after a cross into the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross into goal' reads as a football move, but the cross and the odd letters together go inside a word for an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand is to grow or become larger, which is one sense of develop.

clue.text: Awful Prime Minister is, alas, ultimately missing opposition to growth?

indicators.note: each of the preceding words lacks its ultimate, that is final, letter
awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: Prime without its last letter
Minister without its last letter
is without its last letter
alas without its last letter

explanation.surface: Lament for a dreadful Prime Minister who ends up resisting economic growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a PM opposed to growth, a familiar political jibe; the growth meant is an empire's.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-imperialism opposes expanding an empire's territory, so it is opposition to imperial growth; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Relocate to protect independent American cinema

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one phrase wraps around the other letter

blocks.note: to relocate is to move house
standard abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A small independent American cinema relocating to safeguard its future.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes into the first word of the phrase, between MOV and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Movie house is the US term for a building where films are shown, which is a cinema.

clue.text: Make merry as poet gets a drink for everyone in shed

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so the named letters are dropped from the poet

blocks.note: Philip Larkin, English poet
these letters are the ones to be removed
taken as written
a round is a set of drinks bought for the whole group

explanation.surface: A poet celebrates by buying the whole group a drink in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In shed' reads as a location, but it is an instruction: the poet sheds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark around is to play about and have fun, a synonym of making merry.

clue.text: Sailor into the water – wanting a river to get clean

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the phrase goes without the letter named

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
falling over the side of a ship sends you into the water
r is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A sailor jumps into the water, without a river nearby, to wash himself clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The R removed is the one in OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board means honest and open, with nothing hidden, which is what clean means of a deal or record.

clue.text: See 15
Wall Street's conclusion after forging a paper

indicators.note: forging means faking or hammering into a new shape, so these letters are reworked
a conclusion is the end, so only the last letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
final letter of Street

explanation.surface: Wall Street's end came after someone forged a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wall Street' reads as one name, but Wall is the definition and Street gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: See 4
Escape in sports car perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of sports, all of car and the start of perhaps

explanation.surface: A getaway made in a sports car, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarper is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is to flee or run off quickly, a colloquial synonym of escape.

clue.text: Suit pursuing net damages somehow getting result from court

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal suit chasing net damages somehow yields a verdict in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal words (suit, damages, court) all mislead: court is a tennis court. 'Pursuing' puts the suit word after the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Game, set and match is the umpire's call at the end of a tennis match, the final result on court.

clue.text: Using rag as well for ink

blocks.note: tat is shabby rags or junk
too means as well

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped newspaper using a rag-like scrap as a substitute for ink.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink someone, in informal use, is to tattoo them.

clue.text: Play securing new award

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to play with is to toy
standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A new stage play wins an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is the theatre in the surface, but here it is the verb toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tony is the American award for Broadway theatre, which fits the play in the surface.

clue.text: Computer equipment from any other business in recession on main road

standard abbreviation for road

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main road' reads as one thing, but the two words split, with the reversed agenda item sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard is the set of keys used to type input into a computer, a piece of its hardware.

clue.text: Politician supporting closures from January to March

indicators.note: closures are endings, so the final letters of the next words are taken

blocks.note: last letters of January and to
Member of Parliament

explanation.walkthrough: 'From January to March' looks like a date range, but March is the definition; in a down clue 'supporting' puts MP underneath. Yomp is British military slang.

clue.text: Wrong about following number 20's sport

indicators.note: about means turning round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: ten is a number
a sin is a wrong

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to the answer at 20-across, whose phrase is called in this sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Game, set and match is announced at the end of a tennis match, so tennis is the sport of that phrase.

clue.text: Votes against adopting explosive candidates

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one word is placed inside the other
